record.original_question: Let ξ be a diffuse random measure on a locally compact second countable Abelian group G, and let X be a random element in a G-space. Mass-stationarity means that the origin is a typical location in the mass of ξ, and for simple point processes it is characterized by the shift-invariance condition θ_−T(X, ξ) ≐ (X, ξ) for every measurable shift T = π(X, ξ) induced by a preserving allocation. When ξ is diffuse, is mass-stationarity of (X, ξ) already equivalent to this condition (4.1) without adjoining an extra stationary random field Y independent of (X, ξ)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a locally compact second countable Abelian group with Haar measure $\lambda$, acting measurably on a measurable space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F})$ by shifts $\{\theta_t : t \in G\}$. Let $\xi$ be a random measure on $G$ defined on $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$, and let $X$ be a random element taking values in a measurable $G$-space, so that $(X, \xi)$ carries a natural shift action $\theta_t(X, \xi)$.

Assume $\xi$ is diffuse (i.e.\ $\xi(\{t\}) = 0$ almost surely for every $t \in G$).

A measurable map $\pi$ from the state space of $(X, \xi)$ to $G$ is called a preserving allocation if it produces shifts $T = \pi(X, \xi)$ that preserve the joint distribution in the appropriate balanced sense (the shift $\theta_{-T}$ moves the origin to a point of $\xi$-mass selected in a translation-equivariant way).

Consider the condition
$$\theta_{-T}(X, \xi) \stackrel{d}{=} (X, \xi) \qquad \text{for every shift } T = \pi(X, \xi) \text{ induced by a preserving allocation.} \tag{$\ast$}$$

The pair $(X, \xi)$ is called mass-stationary if, for every relatively compact Borel set $C \subset G$,
$$(\theta_{-V_C}(X, \xi),\, V_C + U_C) \stackrel{d}{=} ((X, \xi),\, U_C),$$
where $U_C$ is uniformly distributed on $C$ independently of $(X, \xi)$ and $V_C$ is sampled from $\xi(\cdot \cap (U_C + C)) / \xi(U_C + C)$ on the event $\{\xi(U_C + C) \in (0, \infty)\}$.

It is known that, when one adjoins a stationary random field $Y$ on $G$ independent of $(X, \xi)$, mass-stationarity of $(X, \xi)$ is equivalent to condition $(\ast)$ holding for $((X, Y), \xi)$.

Question: If $\xi$ is diffuse, is mass-stationarity of $(X, \xi)$ already equivalent to condition $(\ast)$ for $(X, \xi)$ itself, without the auxiliary independent stationary field $Y$?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface foundational work by Last and Thorisson on mass-stationarity and invariant transports, and subsequent papers on stationary and mass-stationary random measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and on transportation of diffuse random measures, but none explicitly announce a resolution of the specific question of whether, for diffuse $\xi$, mass-stationarity is equivalent to the shift-invariance condition under preserving allocations without an auxiliary independent stationary field. The status appears to remain unresolved in the indexed literature.

status_evidence.title: Invariant transports of stationary random measures and mass-stationarity
status_evidence.snippet: Last and Thorisson study invariant transport-kernels balancing stationary random measures on locally compact Abelian groups and introduce mass-stationarity.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational source for the mass-stationarity framework used in the problem, with no resolution of the diffuse-case equivalence.

status_evidence.title: Construction and Characterisation of Stationary and Mass-Stationary Random Measures on R^d
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent characterizations of mass-stationary random measures on R^d.
status_evidence.claim: Later work continues to characterize mass-stationarity but does not announce a resolution of the specific diffuse-case Problem 4.1.

status_evidence.title: Transportation of diffuse random measures on R^d
status_evidence.snippet: Allocations transporting a diffuse source random measure to an arbitrary destination.
status_evidence.claim: Related developments on the diffuse case do not appear to settle the precise equivalence question.
